channel.title: DevCentr Blog
channel.description: Craft, investigations, and orientations from Dev-Centr.

item.title: What a good install actually is
item.description: Installation norms as craft — FHS cargo-cult, Windows honest writes, and a dual-mode layout that might survive connectome-fs.

item.title: MarkView is a good Markdown viewer
item.description: Orientation to MarkView as a free local Markdown viewer (no editing).

item.title: Unifying model runner registration
item.description: Competing unilayer discovery formats punish offline runners. Open Provider Registry should be a shared protocol, not a brand war.

item.title: SoloMD editor: a new Markdown tool to add to your toolbox
item.description: Orientation to SoloMD for local Markdown README and project-doc workflows.

item.title: Auto mode is pricing theater
item.description: Raw frontier APIs blow past a sixty-dollar IDE plan. Harness routing plus a local classify model change the spend curve.

item.title: Why installers wait in line
item.description: Open-source Windows installer tooling copies files well and stalls everywhere else. The global MSI lock is coarse on purpose.

item.title: A harness that does not own the rules
item.description: Direction notes for a T3code-weight local agent runtime — not a News-desk release.

item.title: Architecting your agent rules
item.description: How to structure agent rules so harness quirks stay on the machine — and the templates stay forkable.

item.title: After Skia: rendering for documents that grow
item.description: Electron wins until the document grows. Then the renderer — not the feature list — decides whether the app survives.

item.title: One download, every kernel
item.description: A lab note on single-download packs of native OS/arch slices — not a release announcement.

item.title: Download pages are a design failure
item.description: Almost every compiled program encodes one OS and one CPU. The download page is the scar.

item.title: Stop translating shells
item.description: A playbook should name the outcome. PlayTime binds how on this machine. Equivalence Engine is a catalog — not a bash-to-PowerShell blender.

item.title: OAuth is not a Cloud project
item.description: Personal OAuth does not belong in a Project-shaped box. Consent, quotas, and API enablement are the wrong boundaries.

item.title: Your API key is not a token
item.description: Dashboard secrets keep getting sold as tokens. The wrong word keeps failing security reviews.

item.title: Search the provider, not the scrape
item.description: Vision for provider-native search APIs and API-compatible backups — with a near-term forge archive wedge.
